title: Introduce conditional premerge adaptor and dependency lightening for faster local feedback
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context and motivation: Our presubmit lanes are slow for medium-sized changes because every push triggers a full lint+unit+integration matrix. This increases friction for contributors and drives up CI costs. This PR introduces a conditional premerge adaptor that routes PRs to a lightweight fast-path when changed files match a small deterministic whitelist, and otherwise keeps the existing staged lanes. The branch also includes a one-off dependency lightening step: we split devdeps into "fast-dev" vs "heavy-dev" groups and make the heavy group optional for fast-path runs so local and CI fast-feedback is substantially quicker.

What this change does (summary): Adds a new GitHub Actions composite called .github/actions/conditional-premerge that inspects the changed paths and repo metadata, decides whether to run the fast-path, and injects a curated test matrix. Introduces a small YAML manifest at .ci/fastpath-manifest.yml that lists directories and file globs eligible for fast feedback. Moves heavy dev dependencies into package subsets for npm and a separate go tooling profile for make/golangson. Updates the main presubmit workflow to call the adaptor and fall back to the full staged lanes when necessary.

Design decisions: - Fast-path decisions are purely path-based and deterministic (no heuristics). That keeps correctness simple and debuggable. - We keep the fallback to staged lanes to preserve safety for complex changes. - Dependency lightening is opt-in per-run: the adaptor sets an environment flag (FASTPATH=true) that job entrypoints honor to skip heavy bootstrap steps. - No runtime compilation/serving code changed in this PR; infra-only.

Files affected (high-level): - .github/workflows/presubmit.yml: wire adaptor and new job entries - .github/actions/conditional-premerge/action.yml (+ entrypoint.sh): the composite action - .ci/fastpath-manifest.yml: curated globs eligible for fast feedback - devops/tooling/profiles/fast-dev-packages.json and heavy-dev-packages.json - scripts/ci/bootstrap.sh: respect FASTPATH and skip optional installs - docs/dev/ci-fastpath.md: developer-facing docs and troubleshooting - tools/ci/check-manifest.js: small helper to validate manifest entries

Commits (summary): - initial scaffold of conditional-premerge composite and script; add manifest parser - split devdeps into fast/heavy packages and wire bootstrap flag - update presubmit workflow to call adaptor and add fast-path matrix - add validation tests for manifest and unit test to avoid regressions - docs for contributors and upgrade notes

Testing and verification: - Local smoke: ran adaptor against 30 historical PR diffs and verified correct fast-path decisions. - Nightly dry-run: staged workflow used adaptor in dry-run mode for 48h to ensure no false positives. - CI: full CI matrix passed on the merge commit (lint/unit/integration). - Added unit tests for manifest parsing and a small set of integration checks that exercise the FASTPATH flag in containerized runner images.

Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind FASTPATH_ENABLED repo secret (currently true for this rollout). - Observe premerge feedback latency and run-rate for 2 weeks; metrics captured in Console (CI/Presubmit latency dashboard). - If we see >1% false negatives (changed files misclassified) we will revert adaptor and widen manifest.

Developer notes / doc links: - docs/dev/ci-fastpath.md includes how to extend the manifest and how to run the adaptor locally. - Linear: ENG-2143 (fast-path proposal), ENG-2217 (dep split and bootstrap optimization). - Support ticket SUP-4021 tracked a customer incident showing flaky presubmit timeouts that motivated this work.

Checklist: - [x] Composite action implemented and unit tested - [x] Manifest schema + validator added - [x] Presubmit workflow wired to adaptor with safe fallback - [x] Bootstrap script honors FASTPATH - [x] Docs and contributor notes added - [x] Observability hooks (CI labels/annotations) added

Potential follow-ups: - Add a lightweight heuristics mode based on line-count / churn if path-based approach misses cases - Extend to other repos (sdk, examples) with shared manifest registry - Explore caching strategies for heavy-dev packages to further reduce warmup time

Notes on scope: This PR purposefully keeps the decision logic simple to reduce blast radius. Any future heuristics will be gated and accompanied by telemetry.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after two approvals and a successful CI run.

review_thread: Noah Chen (reviewer) on 2026-02-14: Nice approach. Two concerns: manifest maintenance and potential drift when moving files. Can we add an automated PR check that validates manifest entries against actual repo paths?

Asha Patel (author) on 2026-02-14: Good catch — added tools/ci/check-manifest.js and unit test to validate entries; included in CI matrix for presubmit. Added mention in docs about manifest ownership.
Lena Hoffmann (reviewer) on 2026-02-15: The bootstrap changes look safe but the npm split should keep lockfile determinism. How do we preserve package-lock consistency?

Asha Patel (author) on 2026-02-15: We keep a single package-lock.json and generate the fast-dev subset at install time using a deterministic filter script; the lock is unchanged and CI validates lockfile checksum in full runs.
Ravi Kumar (reviewer) on 2026-02-16: Can we add telemetry labels so we can measure fast-path hit/miss rates?
Asha Patel (author) on 2026-02-16: Added CI annotation headers and a lightweight metric emitter to the adaptor that posts to our internal telemetry endpoint (no PII).
notes_after_merge: Fast-path rollout reduced median presubmit feedback time for small PRs from ~14m to ~3.5m in the first 48 hours. CI cost for presubmit jobs decreased ~18% for the first week; ongoing monitoring configured. No misclassification incidents detected in initial rollout window.
release_notes: Introduce a conditional premerge adaptor and dev dependency separation to speed up presubmit feedback for small changes. No change to runtime behavior. See docs/dev/ci-fastpath.md for contributor guidance.
additional_context: This change intentionally avoids heuristic-based triggers to keep behavior predictable.
See ENG-2143 for the proposal, ENG-2217 for dependency work details.
If problems emerge, revert by removing the adaptor call in .github/workflows/presubmit.yml or set FASTPATH_ENABLED=false in repo secrets.
